title: Generic methods on a non-generic enum

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, why must an enum's generic varargs method `of(T... elements)` be declared final to carry @SafeVarargs?

options.text: Constant bodies may not override a varargs method
options.says: The page states no such rule about constant bodies; it says enum methods are not implicitly final, which is exactly why the modifier has to be written.

options.text: The annotation is refused on methods open to overriding
options.says: The page says @SafeVarargs goes only on static, final or private methods and constructors, and enum methods are not implicitly final.

options.text: The annotation is refused on methods that are public
options.says: The page allows it on final methods whatever their access, and its own example is a public final method.

questions.stem: Per this page, when is the type parameter T of a generic enum method such as `<T> T convert(String s, Class<T> type)` resolved?

options.text: At each call, from the arguments passed to it
options.says: The page says type parameters on enum methods are resolved at the call site, not when the enum is declared.

options.text: At the enum's declaration, from its header
options.says: The page says an enum declaration cannot take type parameters at all, and a method's type is resolved per call, not at declaration time.

options.text: In the constant's body, from its own code
options.says: The page says the type is resolved at the call site, so one constant serves Integer and Double callers alike.

concepts: A type parameter on an enum method is resolved at each call site, so one constant serves many types.
@SafeVarargs is legal only on static, final or private methods and constructors, so a generic varargs enum method is declared final.
